newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures ends mixed on rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures ends mixed on rebound.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Friday on a partial technical rebound after successive falls over the past few days, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 3,155 yuan ($380) per tonne, losing 15 yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 3,150 and hit a high of 3,157 yuan per tonne.
July fell three to 3,152, November rose 20 to 3,165, the January 1998 contract lost 10 to 3,140 and March rose 80 to 3,150. Combined volume rose to 23,700 tonnes from 19,500 tonne.
Soybeans opened mixed and moved around the opening level for most of the session, traders said.
"Some investors liquidated their short positions at low levels due to heavy profits derived from heavy losses over the past few days," one trader said.
"But market sentiment did not improve because of poor domestic fundamentals," he added.
Investors preferred not to take physical delivery in summer, limiting any potential for short term rises, traders said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to consolidate in the next few days.
